- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp price spikes in history, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends; fails to mean-revert quickly when prices fall sharply.
- Forecast bias is stronger in high-price regimes (e.g., >65) than in low-price regimes (<60).
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward corrections.
- Forecasts show persistent overconfidence in upward momentum, especially when history includes recent gains.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to over-forecast the continuation, ignoring potential reversal.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, leading to underprediction of price spikes or drops.
